name: Two-Arm Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
description: The two-arm dumbbell bent-over row is performed identically to the barbell bent-over row, but with two dumbbells instead of a barbell. The independent dumbbells allow each arm to move through its natural path, reducing stress on the wrists and elbows compared to a fixed-bar variation. This version allows greater individual limb accountability and can help address left-right strength imbalances.

execution.starting_position: Hold a dumbbell in each hand. Hinge at the hips to 45 degrees of forward lean with a neutral spine. Let both dumbbells hang at arm's length.
execution.setup_instructions: Choose matching dumbbells. The bilateral version requires greater torso stability than the single-arm variation.
steps: Step 1: Hinge at hips to roughly 45 degrees, dumbbells hanging straight down.
Step 2: Retract scapulae and pull both dumbbells simultaneously toward the lower ribcage.
Step 3: Keep elbows close to the body or allow slight flare based on grip position.
Step 4: Squeeze the lats and rhomboids hard at the top.
Step 5: Lower both dumbbells under control to full extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before each rep. Exhale on the row.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back due to hamstring tightness
Using momentum by rocking the torso
Allowing the elbows to flare too wide, shifting from a lat-focused to rear-delt-focused pull
safety_considerations: Maintain neutral spine throughout — reduce weight if the lower back rounds
Hamstring flexibility determines hip hinge depth; do not force depth beyond neutral spine
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Dumbbells hang at full arm extension at the bottom, pulled to lower ribcage at the top.
coaching_cues: Hinge and hold — no torso bounce
